scope_assessment.title: Code-WTF-StaffAppReviewChecklist-May2017.pdf
scope_assessment.geographic_institutional_scope: City Albuquerque wireless telecommunications zoning administration
scope_assessment.specific_albuquerque_connection: Interprets former Albuquerque Zoning Code section 14-16-3-17, effective December 22, 2014, for City wireless-facility review.
scope_assessment.potential_abqinfo_public_information_val: Ten pages of code-specific criteria may explain historical wireless-facility regulation beyond the blank application form.
scope_assessment.reason_does_not_confidently_pass: Staff routing, fill-in questions and procedural checks dominate parts of the record; final regulations may provide the same reader value more directly.
scope_assessment.reason_does_not_clearly_fail: The checklist interprets a named local zoning section in substantive detail, rather than providing only generic or statewide paperwork.
scope_assessment.substantive_rationale: Specific Albuquerque legal criteria and credible regulatory information coexist with internal applicant-processing content. Owner editorial significance judgment should determine retention; successful retrieval alone is insufficient.

code-enforcement-cluster-research-2026-09-11 integration: A hybrid record that the directory precedent does not settle. It runs ten pages and 23,168 characters and states it is "based on section 14-16-3-17 ROA 1994, most recent revision effective December 22, 2014", so it documents how the City applies a named zoning-code section to wireless telecommunications facilities, which reads as a durable enforcement standard. Against that, it is written as an internal staff routing sheet with fill-in blanks such as "Are there any comments from the City Engineer that the applicant needs to address?", and the Planning UDD artifact recommends excluding Form P1 and Form P3 review checklists. Decide whether staff review checklists that interpret a specific code section are retained as standards or excluded with applicant forms.
